questions.q: Sita's house faces south. She leaves by the back door, walks 50 m straight ahead, turns right and walks 30 m. In which direction is she walking now?
questions.why: The back of the house faces north. She walks north, and a right turn takes her east.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 7, 14, 13, 20, 19, …
questions.why: Alternately add 7 and subtract 1. Next: 26. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In a certain language 'sun rises east' is written 'pa ko ti', 'east or west' is written 'ti la mu' and 'sun sets west' is written 'pa ru la'. Which word means 'rises'?
questions.why: 'pa' is sun (first and third phrases) and 'ti' is east (first and second), so the remaining word 'ko' is rises.

questions.q: Pointing to a woman, Asha (a man) said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the woman related to Asha?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Sister. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Pointing to a woman, Suresh (a man) said, "She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son." How is the woman related to Suresh?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Sister. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The sum of the present ages of a father and son is 60. Six years ago the father was five times as old as the son. What will the son's age be after 6 years?
questions.why: f + s = 60 and f − 6 = 5(s − 6), so s = 14 now and 20 in six years. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Kavita walks 8 m North, then turns left and walks 4 m, then turns right and walks 4 m. Which direction is Kavita facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the North. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Ten years ago Sitamma was three times Radha's age. In ten years she will be twice Radha's age. What is the ratio of their present ages?
In a group of 70 people, 35 like tea, 24 like coffee and 27 like neither. How many like only tea?
questions.why: Both = 35 + 24 − (70 − 27) = 16; only tea = 35 − 16 = 19. GPSC-style practice item.
